## what you are asked
Mark **one** register of **one** comparison of **one** cell. You are shown one register's definition and you may not trade it against another; no call sees a second register, and the registers are never summed, averaged, weighted, ranked or reduced to one mark.

The two sides are shown as `A` and `B`. Nothing here says which side is which arm, and this pack's presentation order is recorded outside it: the same comparison is put to you in both orders, and a mark that changes with the order is not a mark.

`differs` only where this register's definition says the two sides differ, with the closed `difference_kind` token that names how. Quote the two sides you read. Where you cannot tell, answer `unresolved`: absent data is reported as absent data and never as an absence of difference.

## the reading rubric of std:reading-rubric/v1 (contrast-mark, pairwise mode)
question: On this one register and this one case pair, does the successor's commitment surface differ in a way the within-ORIGINAL replicate baseline does not already show?
mode: pairwise

M1. The mode is pairwise: one cell, one comparison, one register, one call. No call sees
    a second register, so no call can trade one register off against another.
M2. The marks are `differs`, `same` and `unresolved`. The register definitions are PLAN
    §8a's own, mirrored byte-identically and not paraphrased here.
M3. The four registers are reported separately and stand or fall separately. They are
    never summed, averaged, weighted, ranked or reduced to one mark (FW5:851).
M4. A mark is not a quantity, and no count of marks warrants anything (FW5:851). Counts
    may defeat; they never warrant.
M5. The within-ORIGINAL baseline is written first and is not revised afterwards. A
    `differs` is admissible only if its `difference_kind` token is absent from the frozen
    baseline's kind set for that register; where the token is present the program writes
    `same` and records the baseline replicate pair that forced it.
M6. Register E: a bare id token shared with the account document is `unresolved` for that
    register and never `differs`.
M7. Absent data is reported as absent data. Fewer than three resolved replicates of a
    case yields no mark for that case; it is reported unresolved, never as an absence of
    difference.
M8. Where two readers disagree on a register, that register is `unresolved` for that cell
    and the disagreement is recorded, never averaged (FW5:634).

## the one register under this mark: G
register G: grounds cited

PLAN §8a, verbatim:

* **G — grounds cited.** Whether the successor grounds that disposition in the
  objection's grounds, the account's, the rival's, or none. `differs` iff the cited
  source of grounds is not the same.

what it reads: Whether the successor grounds that disposition in the objection's grounds, the account's, the rival's, or none.
differs iff: the cited source of grounds is not the same

the closed `difference_kind` tokens for this register, and no others:
- `grounds_source` — The cited source of grounds is not the same.

No mark is a quantity. The four registers are never summed, averaged, weighted, ranked or reduced to a single mark (FW5:851; PURPOSE.md, "no scalar progress meter").

## side A

the objection shows the same report supports alternatives; the rival adds a second axis.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o1","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r2"]},{"id":"s2","type":"claim","text":"The account's test - whether two or three specified chores stop recurring - has low discriminating power unless it is paired with observations of how the withdrawing flatmate responds to the proposal itself and whether recurrence drops on specified items or reappears as new complaint items or after the next schedule change.","scope":"Diagnostic test for the hypotheses in s1.","grounds":"The objection notes that tighter specs on a lopsided arrangement can reduce friction without addressing the driver; the rival proposes reaction-to-proposal as a distinguishing observation.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r7"],"depends":["s1"]},{"id":"s3","type":"claim","text":"The rival's unit-versus-private-lives axis is a live second axis worth testing, but it is not established by the material and should not replace the ambiguity hypothesis.","scope":"This household, given withdrawal from the conversations.","grounds":"The rival concedes the reading is a conjecture; the objection's self-caution and the rival's r9 warn against over-reading.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r3","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r4","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o4"]},{"id":"s4","type":"use","text":"Run a time-boxed diagnostic trial rather than adopting either the account's sequence or the rival's sequence wholesale.","action":"Choose two or three recurring chores; draft done/by-when/fallback for each; hold separate low-pressure conversations rather than one group settlement meeting; observe content-engagement versus pullback from the proposal itself; track recurrence over about two weeks.","consequence":"Content-engagement and falling recurrence support the ambiguity reading. Pullback from the idea of a written arrangement supports the unit/privacy or procedural reading. New complaint items or recurrence after schedule changes support load imbalance or renegotiation/legitimacy.","depends":["s1","s2","s3","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r6","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r7"]},{"id":"s5","type":"commitment","text":"Keep the separate conversations separate until the diagnostic trial has produced a pattern; do not aggregate them immediately into a household-wide settlement.","scope":"If s4 is pursued.","action":"Do not turn the individual conversations into a ratification meeting in the first pass.","consequence":"Preserves the chance of hearing a divergent reading that a group setting may suppress.","depends":["s4","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r10","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c3"]},{"id":"s6","type":"commitment","text":"If the proposal itself is rejected, or if low-pressure attempts still yield withdrawal, shift from specification to truce-shaped arrangements and then name the living-arrangement question explicitly.","scope":"Contingent on s4 failing one or two low-pressure attempts.","action":"Try owned zones or a rotation with a default outcome that nobody has to negotiate in the moment; if engagement still fails, raise lease/living-arrangement fit rather than deferring it.","consequence":"Avoids treating a household-form disagreement as a chore failure and puts the larger decision on the table without forcing it from a chore dispute.","depends":["s4","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r8","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r11"]},{"id":"s7","type":"objection","text":"This synthesis may over-diagnose. Asking what the flat is meant to be can itself escalate the conflict, and the unit/privacy axis can be used to shield a flatmate who simply does not want to do a fair share.","target":["s4","s6","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r9"],"bearing":"If the diagnostic conversation increases withdrawal, the test is not neutral; s4 and s6 should be abandoned or narrowed in that case."},{"id":"s8","type":"problem","text":"What the recurring chores are, how long the pattern has run, what the withdrawing flatmate has said privately, and which reading the flatmates actually hold remain open.","scope":"Material limitations.","mentions":["s1","s2","s3","s4"]},{"id":"s9","type":"claim","text":"The account's concrete safeguards remain useful across all readings: start with two or three recurring items, treat the written note as a draft rather than a contract, avoid moral language about pulling weight, avoid one big settling meeting, and avoid counting instances in the moment.","scope":"Practical chore negotiation in this flat.","grounds":"These moves are cheap, reversible, and do not require adopting the ambiguity hypothesis as established.","target":["daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#u1"]}],"uptake":["s1","s2","s3","s4","s5","s6","s7","s8","s9","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/account#c2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/objection#o2","daily/mini_fcl/cycle-1/rival#r7"]}

## side B
{"language":"FCL-1","records":[{"id":"s1","type":"claim","text":"The account's spec-first order and the rival's existence-first order converge on the same terminal question — whether the living arrangement still fits — so the live disagreement is over which middle steps shape the conversation first, not over the endpoint.","scope":"As both proposals are written.","grounds":"Each names the lease or living-arrangement question as the point at which chores stop being the issue."},{"id":"s2","type":"claim","text":"The recurrence test should be revised rather than abandoned: record what the next disagreement is about as well as whether one occurs. 'We never settled that' favours ambiguity; 'that was before my shifts changed' favours renegotiation; 'why are you the one raising this' favours standing or legitimacy.","scope":"Any trialled chore specification.","grounds":"Bare recurrence is compatible with every reading, but content is nearly free to record and separates them."},{"id":"s3","type":"claim","text":"Reviewing two or three specific past disagreements for what the disagreement actually was discriminates ambiguity, renegotiation and standing better than trialling a remedy and watching recurrence does, and it can be done with the flatmates who are still talking.","scope":"This household, on the material available.","grounds":"The three readings predict different contents for a dispute about the same event, and the account's own test was criticised precisely for not distinguishing them."},{"id":"s4","type":"claim","text":"The rival's proposed discriminator is one-sided: engagement with the content of a proposed specification is informative, but withdrawal from the proposal itself is not, because withdrawal is equally predicted by a lopsided load, a history of being audited, or impatience with being managed.","scope":"Rival r7, and any diagnosis that treats resistance to explicitness as evidence for a unit-versus-privacy reading.","mentions":["rival#r7","rival#r9"]},{"id":"s5","type":"claim","text":"A private fortnight census of who actually does what is cheap, needs no agreement from the withdrawing flatmate, and separates a two-to-one load split from an ambiguity problem as well as anything either proposal offers.","scope":"Shared-household chores.","consequence":"If the census shows a stable lopsided split, the ambiguity-first reading should be dropped rather than repaired. It is for the person keeping it, not for presenting as evidence."},{"id":"s6","type":"objection","text":"The objection's complaint about ordering is fair as a caution and weak as an argument: anyone intending to act has a sequence, including the objection, whose preferred reordering puts the conversational-form reading first on the same thin material.","target":["objection#o3"],"bearing":"If it holds, o3 reduces to a demand that any sequence be cheap to reverse, which is weaker than reshuffling it."},{"id":"s7","type":"objection","text":"The rival reading risks self-sealing: under r9's own warning, resistance to explicitness counts as evidence for the unit-versus-privacy reading while being exactly what free-riding, load resentment or conflict fatigue would produce. No test the person can defeat by declining to participate can carry that weight.","target":["rival#r7","rival#r9"],"bearing":"The unit-versus-privacy axis remains a live competitor but does not become the front-runner on this evidence."},{"id":"s8","type":"objection","text":"The rival's opening move asks the least available flatmate an abstract, high-stakes question in a vocabulary the flatmates have not used — what is this flat — and is easily heard as a prelude to a lease conversation.","target":["rival#r6"],"bearing":"Supports demoting it: ask about the last disagreement rather than the nature of the household, and only if the person will talk at all."},{"id":"s9","type":"use","text":"Gather cheap evidence before proposing any written arrangement: review two or three past disagreements for content with the flatmates who are still talking; keep a private fortnight census of who does what; then make one narrow one-to-one approach about one concrete item.","action":"Do the review and the census this week; do the one-to-one approach only after, and once. Do not open with a shared note or a general household conversation.","consequence":"The reading that gets adopted is chosen on evidence rather than on which proposal was read first.","depends":["s2","s3","s5"]},{"id":"s10","type":"use","text":"Keep one-to-one contact one-to-one in both directions: do not aggregate it straight into a group decision, and do not let it harden into a two-person understanding the third discovers later.","action":"Say which parts of a one-to-one conversation may be raised with the others and which may not.","consequence":"Prevents a private alliance forming in place of the group negotiation.","revises":["rival#r10"]},{"id":"s11","type":"use","text":"If a specification is trialled at all, trial one item only and pre-commit to how a recurrence at the next schedule change will be read — as evidence for renegotiation, not as the item's failure or someone's bad faith.","action":"Name that reading before the trial starts.","consequence":"Prevents the trial being scored after the fact in whatever direction suits whoever scores it.","depends":["s2"]},{"id":"s12","type":"problem","text":"Nothing in the material says what the chores are, how long the pattern has run, whether the withdrawing flatmate has given a reason, or whether the other two agree about why the withdrawal happened. The withdrawal is treated by all three inputs as central and is the one thing nobody has explained.","mentions":["account#c1","objection#p1","rival#r5"]},{"id":"s13","type":"commitment","text":"If the census shows a stable two-to-one split in who actually does the work, drop the ambiguity-first reading rather than repairing it, and start the conversation from the split.","scope":"Conditional on s5 being carried out and producing that result.","action":"Set the specification proposal aside for that round.","consequence":"Avoids spending the household's remaining goodwill on clearer paperwork for a lopsided arrangement.","depends":["s5"]},{"id":"s14","type":"commitment","text":"If the case review finds a mixed pattern — some disputes about what was meant, some about changed circumstances, some about who may raise the matter — treat the plurality as the finding and move to truce-shaped arrangements that require agreement on less rather than more.","scope":"Conditional on s3 producing a mixed pattern.","action":"Owned zones, or rotations with an un-negotiated default.","consequence":"Addresses load and exposure without requiring the flatmates to settle what kind of household this is.","depends":["s3"],"mentions":["rival#r8"]},{"id":"s15","type":"claim","text":"The narrow one-to-one approach to the withdrawing flatmate is the piece of the account least dependent on which diagnosis is right, and it survives the ambiguity, renegotiation, standing and unit-versus-privacy readings alike.","scope":"As first contact, not as settlement.","grounds":"Every reading predicts such an approach is at least not worse than a general conversation; none predicts it works on its own."}],"uptake":["s2","s3","s5","s9","s10","s11","s13","s14","s15","account#c3","objection#o2","rival#r8","rival#r9"]}
